subcategory: Responsible AI, Human Rights and Safety
oneSentence: Confidentiality means limiting access to information so only authorised people can see, use or share it for a legitimate purpose.
plainExplanation:
Some information should not be openly shared. That can include personal details, health records, legal files, security plans, interview notes, or draft decisions. Confidentiality is the rule and practice of keeping that information restricted to the right people for the right reason.

What goes in is information that could cause harm, unfairness, loss of trust, or safety risks if exposed. Then people and systems apply controls such as access limits, need-to-know rules, careful storage, and safe sharing procedures. What comes out should be useful work without unnecessary exposure of the information.

In AI work, confidentiality matters at every stage: collecting data, preparing prompts, training or testing systems, storing outputs, and sharing results. If staff paste sensitive material into an unapproved public AI service, they may lose control over who can access it or how it is used. Even a summary can break confidentiality if it reveals protected facts.

Confidentiality is often confused with privacy and data security, but they are not the same. Privacy is about a person’s rights and appropriate use of information about them. Data security is about protecting information from loss, theft, or unauthorised access. Confidentiality is the rule that some information must only be available to authorised people, even if the system is technically secure.

everydayAnalogy.title: A sealed envelope for the right desk
everydayAnalogy.story: At a food distribution point, a coordinator writes tomorrow’s delivery plan. One page lists general stock numbers for all volunteers. A second page contains the names and phone numbers of two drivers and the exact time a high-value shipment will arrive. That second page goes into a sealed envelope addressed only to the transport lead, while the general stock page goes on the notice board. The work continues, but only the people who need the sensitive page can open it.

mapping.analogyElement: The transport lead named on the envelope
mapping.aiElement: Authorised person with a legitimate need to know

mapping.analogyElement: The public stock page on the notice board
mapping.aiElement: Information that can be shared more widely
Separating confidential data from general operational data

everydayAnalogy.limitation: Real confidentiality is not only about putting something in a hidden place. It also includes rules about collection, copying, onward sharing, retention, logging, and disposal. In digital systems, a person might access data without physically opening anything, and confidential information can sometimes be inferred from small clues spread across several documents.

visual.title: How confidential information should move through an AI-related task
visual.learningObjective: Show how information should be checked, limited, handled, and shared so sensitive details do not spread beyond authorised users.
visual.description: A left-to-right step diagram with four boxes connected by arrows. Each box shows one stage in handling information before, during, and after AI use. Read from identifying sensitive content to limiting access, using approved tools, and sharing only the minimum necessary result.

steps.label: 1. Identify
steps.explanation: Check whether the material includes personal, protection-sensitive, legal, medical, financial, security, or other restricted information.
steps.visualInstruction: Draw a document icon with highlighted lines and small tags reading personal, legal, security.

steps.label: 2. Limit access
steps.explanation: Decide who genuinely needs the information for the task. Others should not receive it.
steps.visualInstruction: Show three person icons; only one is linked to the document with a solid line, the others with faded lines.

steps.label: 3. Use approved handling
steps.explanation: If AI is used, use only approved tools and remove or mask unnecessary sensitive details where possible.
steps.visualInstruction: Show the document moving into a checked box labelled approved tool; redacted black bars cover some text.

steps.label: 4. Share minimum output
steps.explanation: Release only the result needed for the job, not the full sensitive source material.
steps.visualInstruction: Show a short summary card leaving the approved tool, while the original full document stays behind a lock icon.

visual.interaction: Hover or tap each step to reveal an example of what should and should not be shared at that stage.
visual.accessibilityDescription: This diagram explains confidentiality as a four-step process. Step 1: identify whether information is sensitive, such as personal, legal, medical, financial, or security-related details. Step 2: limit access to people with a real need to know. Step 3: if AI is used, use only approved tools and remove unnecessary sensitive details where possible. Step 4: share only the minimum result needed, not the full original material. The main message is that confidentiality is maintained by checking the information, restricting who can access it, handling it through approved channels, and avoiding oversharing.
visual.reducedMotionDescription: A static four-step horizontal diagram with labelled boxes and arrows. No animation. Each step remains visible at once, showing identify, limit access, use approved handling, and share minimum output.

workedExample.scenario: A team wants AI help to draft a short briefing about medicine deliveries to three clinics.
workedExample.input: Raw notes include clinic names, medicine quantities, driver phone numbers, warehouse location, and one line naming a patient linked to a special delivery.
process: The officer reviews the notes and marks the patient name, driver phone numbers, and warehouse location as confidential for this task.
Instead of pasting the raw notes into an unapproved tool, the officer prepares a cleaned version with clinic labels A, B, and C and keeps only medicine quantities and delivery dates.
The approved tool is asked to draft a neutral summary from the cleaned text.
The officer checks the draft to make sure no hidden identifiers or sensitive operational details remain before sharing it.
workedExample.result: The final briefing says: Clinic A receives 240 treatment packs on Monday, Clinic B 180 on Tuesday, and Clinic C 120 on Tuesday. It contains no patient name, no phone numbers, and no precise warehouse location.

unWorkplaceExample.scenario: A procurement team is preparing requirements for a software purchase and wants AI help to tidy the wording of the statement of work.
unWorkplaceExample.relevance: Confidentiality matters because draft procurement documents may include budget ranges, supplier-sensitive comparisons, internal evaluation methods, or security requirements that should be seen only by authorised staff.
unWorkplaceExample.caution: Do not paste confidential procurement drafts, vendor submissions, internal scoring notes, personal data, or security-sensitive requirements into an unapproved public AI service. Use approved tools and share only the minimum text needed.

whyItMatters: Confidentiality protects people, operations, trust, and fairness. If sensitive information is exposed, people can be harmed, negotiations can be affected, security can be weakened, and organisations can lose credibility. In AI-related work, mistakes can spread quickly because tools make copying, summarising, and sharing very easy. For a non-specialist, the key decision is simple: before using or sharing information, ask who needs it, what can be removed, which tool is approved, and whether the output reveals more than it should. Confidentiality is not only a legal or technical issue; it is a practical check on responsible judgement.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: If information is stored in a password-protected system, confidentiality is fully solved.
commonMisconceptions.correction: A password helps, but confidentiality also depends on who is allowed to access the information, whether they have a legitimate purpose, what they copy or share, and whether the information is minimised. A secure system can still be used in a way that exposes confidential material to the wrong people.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Removing names always makes information safe to share.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Names are only one identifier. A person or place can still be recognised from job title, location, dates, rare events, phone numbers, or combinations of details. Confidentiality may still be broken if a summary or dataset allows someone to infer who is involved.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confidentiality is the same as privacy.
commonMisconceptions.correction: They are related but different. Privacy concerns people’s rights and appropriate handling of information about them. Confidentiality is a restriction on who may access or share certain information. Some confidential information is not personal, such as internal bidding strategies or security layouts.

simpleVsTechnical.simple: Keep sensitive information only with the people who truly need it, and do not put it into tools or channels that are not approved.
simpleVsTechnical.technical: Confidentiality is an information-governance principle and control objective that restricts access, use, disclosure, and onward transfer of protected information to authorised parties for specified purposes. In practice it is maintained through classification, need-to-know access, role-based permissions, contractual and professional duties, approved processing environments, minimisation, redaction, logging, retention limits, and review before disclosure. In AI workflows, confidentiality risk can arise during data collection, prompt entry, model training or fine-tuning, retrieval from connected sources, output generation, storage, human review, and sharing. The concept overlaps with privacy and security but is not identical to either: privacy focuses on rights and appropriate processing of personal data, while security covers safeguards against unauthorised access, alteration, or loss. Confidentiality specifically concerns whether information is exposed beyond those authorised to receive it.

keyTakeaway: Before using AI or sharing a document, ask: who truly needs this information, and what can be removed so sensitive details stay protected?

quickCheck.question: Which action best protects confidentiality in an AI-related task?
options: Paste the full case file into any chatbot, then delete the chat afterwards.
Share the raw document with the whole team so everyone can spot problems.
Use an approved tool and remove names, contact details, and other unnecessary sensitive details before submitting text.
Rely on the AI tool to decide which parts are confidential.
quickCheck.explanation: The best answer is to use an approved tool and minimise the information first. Deleting a chat later may not remove earlier exposure. Sharing raw files widely breaks need-to-know. An AI tool should not be relied on by itself to recognise all confidential material; human review is still needed.
